declared_purpose: FreeRide configures OpenClaw to use ranked free OpenRouter models with fallbacks, preserving unrelated configuration. Optional live rotation and a watcher support recovery from failures. The entry document requires an OpenRouter credential and declares local configuration, cache and watcher-state writes; attribution headers, credential display and detailed logging are implementation choices.

data_operations.source: Shared main.py credential loader used by the CLI and watcher
data_operations.data_scope: One or multiple OPENROUTER_API_KEY credentials; the complete OpenClaw configuration is parsed when the environment value is absent.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling process memory; no remote disclosure occurs in this loader.
data_operations.condition: Credential-dependent commands and probes; the environment takes precedence over env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.

data_operations.operation: Instruct credential display and optional persistence
data_operations.data_scope: The complete OPENROUTER_API_KEY environment value; optionally the supplied credential for persistent configuration.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The echo command's stdout and its caller; optional env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY configuration through the external openclaw command.
data_operations.condition: Following the prerequisite before any FreeRide command; persistence is offered as an option. External command implementation is not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Fetch the model catalog with authentication and application attribution
data_operations.source: main.py fetch_all_models and shared request headers
data_operations.data_scope: Bearer credential, static repository attribution and application title; the response supplies model records. No conversation content is included in this GET.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models; returned records initially remain in caller memory. The repository URL is a header value, not a separate request recipient.
data_operations.condition: A catalog refresh is required or forced and a non-cooling credential is available. Credentials are retried after 401/429; network failures also advance to another key.

data_operations.operation: Filter models and infer ranking scores
data_operations.data_scope: API model IDs, output modalities, pricing, context length, supported parameters, creation time and provider identity; derived _score values concern models, not people.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory, followed by the model cache.
data_operations.condition: A fresh catalog is processed; free text-output models are retained and ranked.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist ranked model records
data_operations.data_scope: Complete retained API model objects, derived _score values and a local cached_at timestamp.
data_operations.condition: Nonempty fresh results overwrite the cache. Non-forced lookups can reuse it for six hours. Expiration rejects reuse; it does not delete the file.

data_operations.source: main.py configuration helpers and configuration-changing commands
data_operations.data_scope: The whole existing JSON document is read and serialized locally. Normal changes set primary/fallback model IDs and allowlist entries. Explicit --setup-auth can additionally create auth.profiles.openrouter:default containing provider and mode, without copying a credential into that profile.
data_operations.condition: Successful auto, switch, fallbacks or rotation paths. Existing allowlist entries are retained. Optional auth-profile creation extends beyond the entry document's advertised model-key-only changes.

data_operations.operation: Display local configuration and credential fragments
data_operations.data_scope: Credential count and, for sufficiently long keys, the first eight and last four characters; auth-profile presence, selected models, cache count/age and the configuration path.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Stdout and the invoking caller, potentially a terminal or agent tool return. Further transmission or retention is not established.
data_operations.condition: freeride status; this handler makes no HTTP request.

data_operations.source: main.py _test_model, invoked by rotate and watcher checks
data_operations.data_scope: Bearer credential, application-attribution headers, target model ID and a fixed synthetic greeting, with max_tokens set to five. Successful generated content is not read or saved; error fields may be parsed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions; downstream provider handling is undocumented in the supplied source.
data_operations.condition: rotate tests the current primary unless forced, then tests candidates when rebuilding. The watcher probes once or repeatedly, defaulting to 60 seconds with a 15-second minimum. Credential retries occur on 401/429.

data_operations.operation: Infer and temporarily retain credential and model health
data_operations.source: main.py request-status handling and watcher rotation logic
data_operations.data_scope: Credential-to-failure timestamps for 401/429, model success/failure codes and rotation reasons.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Process memory; a successful watcher rotation also persists its last reason in watcher state.
data_operations.condition: Relevant request outcomes. Credential cooldown entries are removed lazily when checked after 120 seconds; no credential cooldown file is written.

data_operations.operation: Read, persist and display bounded watcher state
data_operations.source: watcher.py state helpers and status handler
data_operations.data_scope: Rotation count, last successful rotation timestamp and last reason; this is last-event state rather than a growing event history.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/.freeride-watcher-state.json, temporarily its .json.tmp sibling during replacement, and stdout for --status.
data_operations.condition: State is read on watcher startup, one-shot checks or status inspection. Successful rotations update it through temporary-file replacement.

data_operations.operation: Emit watcher diagnostics and optionally persist them
data_operations.source: watcher.py output and the documented background command
data_operations.data_scope: Startup credential count, interval, model IDs, timestamped healthy/failed checks, rotation diagnostics and exception text.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Normally stdout/stderr and their caller; the documented nohup invocation redirects both to ~/.openclaw/freeride-watcher.log.
data_operations.condition: The watcher emits output during execution. File persistence occurs only when the documented redirection or another output collector is used; no log-size or retention control is supplied.

data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/.freeride-watcher-state.json is unlinked; cache, configuration and logs are not covered by this operation.
data_operations.condition: --clear is selected without --status taking precedence. Secure erasure and deletion of copies are not established.

data_operations.data_scope: Badge resource paths; actual request metadata and any viewer linkage depend on the renderer.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Referenced image hosts are api.clawhub-badge.xyz and img.shields.io; a renderer may instead fetch through a proxy.
data_operations.condition: Only if a documentation renderer retrieves embedded images. No corresponding CLI or watcher request is implemented.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Prerequisite command stdout and its terminal or agent caller.
potential_excess.condition: The entry document's echo-based credential check is followed.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The explicit requirement is to establish that a credential is configured; displaying its value is unnecessary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Check for a nonempty credential without revealing it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Replace echo with a presence check that prints only a configured/not-configured result.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve missing-credential guidance and the supported credential sources; no remote validation is needed merely to check presence.

potential_excess.data_scope: First-eight and last-four credential characters for each sufficiently long configured key.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: freeride status stdout and its caller.
potential_excess.condition: Status is requested with configured credentials.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Configuration status and multiple-key visibility require presence/count information; secret-derived identifiers are an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report whether credentials exist and how many are configured.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use ordinal or user-assigned labels instead of credential substrings.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain key count and individual labels where users need to distinguish configured entries. This narrows status output rather than removing the status action.

potential_excess.data_scope: Static repository identity and application title attached to authenticated catalog and probe traffic.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: OpenRouter through HTTP-Referer and X-Title on /api/v1/models and /api/v1/chat/completions.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The source explicitly adds these headers for application attribution. Ranking, configuration and availability testing do not depend on attribution in the supplied implementation.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Fetch model records and send authenticated synthetic probes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit attribution headers by default or make them opt-in.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep authentication, endpoint selection and required request bodies. Confirm external API acceptance because server-side header requirements are not supplied. This removes extra metadata from required requests, not the requests themselves.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete API-supplied free-model objects, including fields unused after ranking; these are catalog metadata, with no user content evidenced.
potential_excess.condition: A refresh produces nonempty ranked results.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Caching supports model selection and listing. Supplied cached-result consumers use model IDs, context lengths and scores rather than complete API records.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain sufficient ranked metadata for the six-hour cache and existing command output.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Persist a projection containing id, context_length and _score alongside cached_at.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue filtering and scoring fresh full records before projection; preserve ordering and all supplied cached-result consumers.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated timestamped successful checks and model IDs, accumulated with other watcher diagnostics.
potential_excess.condition: The background logging example is used during prolonged watcher operation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Autonomous recovery requires periodic probes; persisting every healthy result indefinitely is not required for recovery or the supplied last-rotation status.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep checking health, rotate on failures and expose useful operational status.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Suppress routine successful-check output by default and bound retained diagnostics through log rotation or retention limits.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep probes, failure/rotation diagnostics and watcher-state updates. This narrows optional persistence; it does not remove necessary health checks.

unknowns: OpenRouter retention, application-activity visibility, downstream provider selection and provider handling of synthetic probes are not established by the supplied source.
Whether the catalog endpoint requires authentication or either endpoint requires attribution headers cannot be verified from packaged client code.

OpenClaw source is absent: actual conversation forwarding, runtime fallback/key rotation, credential persistence and gateway behavior remain unresolved. Documentation alone does not establish these external operations.
The watcher rewrites configuration without invoking gateway restart; whether a running gateway adopts those changes is unresolved.
Terminal, agent-tool, supervisor and documentation-renderer retention or forwarding are unspecified. Ordinary stdout/tool returns do not establish third-party disclosure.

Dependency, installer and external command implementations are absent; their additional data operations cannot be audited from this package. File permissions, backups and secure deletion guarantees are also unspecified.
